Mucormycosis: The presence of angioinvasive microbial structures, pauciseptate hyphae, and sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells in the histopathological examination are characteristic of Mucormycosis. The patient's clinical presentation of tender, warm, erythematous nodular skin lesions that progressed to central ulceration with a necrotic core also supports this diagnosis.
Aspergillosis: Although Aspergillosis can also present with similar clinical manifestations, the presence of pauciseptate hyphae and sporangial-type cells in the histopathological examination are more characteristic of Mucormycosis. However, Aspergillosis remains a possible diagnosis due to the patient's immunocompromised state and history of neutropenia.
